home.title: Uttara Farm — Prosperity through turmeric and ginger farming in Vidarbha
home.description: A social initiative supporting farmers in Ralegaon and Vidarbha, Maharashtra with turmeric and ginger expertise, soil testing, and access to major markets.

about.title: Our Story — Vijay Uttarwar & Uttara Farm
about.description: From Bhamb to Naturell, Max Protein, and Zydus Wellness — Vijay Uttarwar’s full-circle journey back to farming communities in Vidarbha through Uttara Farm.

hero.title: Prosperity for farmers through turmeric and ginger
hero.subtitle: We are starting with turmeric and ginger, both high-yield crops with regular demand, and helping farming families in Ralegaon and Vidarbha grow them with expert guidance, practical tools, and fair access to big-city markets.

mission.title: A social project rooted in local farming
mission.p1: Agriculture is the backbone of our region. Uttara Farm exists to help farmers build economic stability from the land they already know—without having to leave it behind.
mission.p2: By starting with high-yield crops like turmeric and ginger and surrounding farmers with training, testing, and market connections, we aim to turn local farming into a more resilient livelihood.

ginger.title: Why turmeric and ginger
ginger.lead: Turmeric and ginger can both deliver strong returns and regular market demand, but they are management-intensive crops that need disciplined execution.
ginger.p1: These crops require careful season-long attention: land preparation, seed quality, nutrition, irrigation, and disease management all matter. That is why going it alone is risky.
ginger.p2: Our programme reduces that risk by pairing farmers with experienced crop advisors, soil insight, and a clearer path from field to buyers in larger cities.

knowledge.title: Knowledge & field guidance
knowledge.body: Hands-on training and season-long advice from turmeric and ginger consultants—including specialists like Nilesh—so practices match local soil and weather.

infrastructure.title: Tools & soil insight
infrastructure.body: Access to soil testing kits and support through Warkem, helping farmers understand their land before they plant and adjust nutrition responsibly.

markets.title: Scale, logistics & markets
markets.body: Working toward better bundling, grading, and transport so produce can reach tier-1 markets such as Mumbai—capturing economies of scale small lots often miss.

region.title: Ralegaon & Vidarbha
region.p1: We work in Ralegaon and the wider Vidarbha region of Maharashtra—communities where farming shapes daily life and seasonal income.
region.p2: Our effort is deliberately local: solutions should fit Vidarbha’s climate, soils, and the realities of family farms.

aboutPage.title: From Bhamb to the world — and back again
aboutPage.lead: Vijay Uttarwar’s journey runs from a farming village in Vidarbha to agriculture college, computer science in America, building Naturell and Max Protein, joining Zydus Wellness — and returning to Bhamb through Uttara Farm.

roots.title: Roots in the land
roots.p1: Eight generations back, the family’s story begins in Uttur, a small village near Hyderabad in Andhra Pradesh. Ancestors migrated into Maharashtra. In Andhra, people were addressed by village name with respect — Uttur Garu. In Maharashtra that became the surname Uttarwar.
roots.p2: Vijay grew up on the family farm in Bhamb. Childhood meant school, farm animals, hide-and-seek, and festivals like Ganesh when the whole village came together. Celebration was never only about the festival — it was about belonging.
roots.p3: With no local doctor or grocery store, his mother’s home became the village pharmacy for first aid. That give-and-take built a culture of oneness: not just family, but the whole village as an extended family.

education.title: Choosing agriculture — and discovering computers
education.p1: His father believed deeply in education. With no school beyond the early grades in the village, Vijay was sent to Nagpur for English-medium schooling — a seventh-grader living in a lodge with a cousin, against his grandfather’s strong opposition. The memories were hard, but lasting.
education.p2: Even as a student he helped his father with farm supervision. Offered both engineering and agriculture, his father let him decide. Heart chose agriculture: BSc from Akola, then MSc in agronomy from Nagpur — university topper and gold medalist.
education.p3: In 1983–84, a single computer behind glass in an air-conditioned room at the agriculture university fascinated him. He learned Fortran on punch cards and used programming for statistical analysis instead of manual calculation — a curiosity that opened the door to computer science in the United States.

america.title: America, marriage, and a decade away
america.p1: US universities admitted him with prerequisites; he finished coursework in two years while taking many extra courses. Life then brought Smita into the story: engaged on 14 January and married four days later — about four thousand guests, made possible by the goodwill of her father’s medical and philanthropic standing.
america.p2: From 1989 to 1999 they built a life in the United States — education, work, and family. Home was never entirely behind them. When they returned to India, adjusting to school and society again was challenging at first, then it settled.

return.title: From software back to the farmer
return.p1: Vijay looks at life as a journey with ups and downs. Moving from the software industry, he wanted to do something for the farmer. Stevia offered many times the income of jowar, cotton, or soybean. Naturell began around that idea: understand demand, then grow supply at the scale the market needed.
return.p2: When regulators said stevia could not be sold as a sweetener unless officially listed, the company already had about forty people. Instead of shutting down, they pivoted into something new — Max Protein — with Smita’s kitchen trials, food technologists, and nearly two years of formulating until Choco Delight, a bar still loved today.

uttara.title: Uttara Farm: making farming viable again
uttara.p1: Yavatmal is too often known for farmer distress. Vijay cannot change everything alone, but he asked what small bit he could do. The core problem is income: when earnings cannot cover debt, pressure becomes unbearable.
uttara.p2: Not all farmers in Maharashtra are poor. Nashik, Pune, Kolhapur, Satara, and Bhusawal show what organised high-value crops and infrastructure can do. Sugar in western Maharashtra and bananas around Bhusawal prove the model. Uttara Farm applies that same thought process locally.
uttara.p3: He looks at farming as industry: expert growing and hand-holding, supply-chain efficiency, and marketing that reaches consumers. Early work with about twenty-five farmers is showing strong crops; the next step is scale through a cooperative or FPO so every last rupee can go to the farmer.
uttara.p4: The larger ambition is reverse migration — retaining talent so graduates earning a modest city salary can live well in the village instead of leaving it behind.

circle.title: Full circle
circle.p1: From small-village Bhamb to Nagpur, to the US, back to Mumbai, and now back to Bhamb — personally and professionally, Vijay’s journey has come full circle. Uttara Farm is where that circle meets the land and the people who shaped him.

brands.title: Naturell, Max Protein, and Zydus Wellness
brands.intro: A regulatory setback on stevia became the turning point for a nutrition brand that scaled nationally — and later found a home with Zydus Wellness.

naturell.title: Naturell
naturell.body: Naturell began with stevia as a higher-income crop for farmers and a consumer sweetener business. When that path was blocked, the team rebuilt around nutrition snacking instead of closing shop.

maxProtein.title: Max Protein
maxProtein.body: Max Protein grew from kitchen trials into a mainstream protein brand. Smita led formulation work — dozens of trials a day — until products like Choco Delight earned lasting consumer love.

zydus.title: Zydus Wellness
zydus.body: The merger with Zydus Wellness marked a new chapter: scale for the brands, and for Vijay and Smita the freedom to return attention to Bhamb and Uttara Farm.
